text:
customer-sre: Customer reported streaming flicker + repeated reconnects on SSE. They see a partial last event then the connection drops after ~62s. Happening across ALB+Cloudflare in front of our hosted API.

elyse: ugh. which customer / request-id? any repro steps?

customer-sre: sent request id r-0a1b2c3d, app stack: frontend->cloudflare->alb->redwood-hosted. Repro with curl:
```
curl -v -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  'https://api.redwood.test/v1/stream?stream_id=abc'
```
I pasted tcpdump + headers: responses start streaming, then after 62s we see TCP FIN from ALB and the client reconnects. No 5xx from origin.

ben: that 62s smells like ALB idle timeout (60s) + a couple seconds of buffering. Cloudflare also has buffering/coalescing behavior when chunks are tiny. Are we sending heartbeats?

customer-sre: customer says they send small heartbeat events every 30s, still hit the drop. They tried increasing app heartbeat to 15s and saw fewer disconnects but still periodic flicker. They also reported billing spikes due to client auto-retries.

dan: ask ops-ingress to check proxy logs + whether gzip/nginx buffering is on for that route. If ALB is in front of Nginx+Envoy that's a chain that can collapse small chunks.

ops-ingress: checking logs now. ALB idle_timeout=60s, Cloudflare proxy in front with Rocket loader off but proxy buffering may be on. Envoy config for the cluster has connection_idle_timeout unset (defaults). We also see Transfer-Encoding: chunked from origin, but response chunk sizes are tiny (~20-40 bytes) for heartbeats. Cloudflare will coalesce small writes into larger TCP segments when TLS record aggregation happens.

elyse: two-pronged workaround: 1) on origin set bigger periodic heartbeat (e.g., 10s) or send fixed-size pad so edge doesn't coalesce 2) set anti-buffering headers when possible: `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for nginx and `Cache-Control: no-transform` to discourage intermediate proxies. Also recommend a short-lived keepalive probe from client (but client reconnects cause billing).

ben: another trick is ensure the first chunk after connection has at least ~1KB payload to avoid some proxies switching to buffered mode. Ugly but sometimes effective.

customer-sre: customer tried adding 512B pad to each heartbeat -> reduced Cloudflare coalescing, but ALB still cuts after 60s if origin is silent. They saw FW logs showing ALB sent FIN after idle.

ops-ingress: we can flip ALB idle timeout higher for the VIP (to 300s) but that's per-load-balancer and may affect other routes. NLB would not do this. For Private/Dedicated customers we can suggest NLB or TCP passthrough to avoid HTTP-level buffering.

dan: file reproducible steps for Eng Runtime. We need a small repro that reproduces the 62s cut using our staging stack with Cloudflare in front of ALB. Capture pcap + proxy traces. Also need to evaluate whether our token/session billing logic double-charges on reconnects.

support-bot: Created support ticket SR-9876 and linked r-0a1b2c3d. Add eng-runtime label and ops-ingress.

elyse: plan for customer: (1) temporary: increase heartbeat to 10s and add 512B pad, (2) ops: set ALB idle_timeout to 300s on their LB or suggest switching to NLB/TCP passthrough, (3) engineering: reproduce on staging with pcap and try `X-Accel-Buffering: no` + disable gzip. Notify customer to pause client auto-retry to avoid billing spike while we triage.

customer-sre: customer ok with trying heartbeat/pad + disable client auto-retry. We'll report back with results in ~2 hours. Thanks all. :pray:

ben: follow-up note for runbook: add checklist for streaming support -> check ALB idle, Cloudflare buffering, `X-Accel-Buffering`, small-chunk padding, and recommend NLB for long-lived streams.

ops-ingress: capturing pcap/traces now, will attach to SR-9876 when done.

elyse: if customer still hits disconnect after the mitigation, escalate to Eng Runtime for deeper kernel/TCP-level trace. Link to internal bug: https://redwood.internal/issue/2345 (added after reproduction).
